first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$705m and adj. EBITDA $117-120m, company guide raised 2026-09-08 (https://www.chime.com/newsroom/chime-announces-agreement-to-acquire-stride-bank/); consensus revenue $705.2m and EPS $0.09 (whisper $0.15) per Earnings Whispers 2026-10-27 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/CHYM/21805), consistent with the guide. FY2026 guide $2.76-2.77bn revenue, adj. EBITDA $481-489m (same Sep 8 release).
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 25,180,963 shares, 7.58% of float, 5.8 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15, down 2.9% from 25,929,970 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CHYM/short-interest, FINRA publication 2026-10-26; Massive.com shows the same 25.18M / 5.8 DTC). Not a crowded short. Baseline skew +10.65 vol points (25d put over call): downside paid; put/call OI 1.08; event-implied move 10.13%, straddle 12.42%. Stock up 6.58% intraday on the print day itself (Massive.com, 2026-11-04 13:02 ET), +4.86% 5d, +8.13% 20d, 12.6% below the 52-week high.

evidence.text: Chime reset its own Q3 guide on 2026-09-08, about two-thirds into the quarter, to revenue ~$705m (from $680-690m) and adj. EBITDA $117-120m (from $105-110m); consensus $705.2m sits exactly on it. On the last print the company beat its own revenue guide midpoint by ~5% ($670m vs $633-643m guide), but a guide set with two months of the quarter in hand leaves room for only a ~1-2% beat (~$710-720m).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): revenue $670m vs $633-643m guide, with a FY raise, stock +20.56%. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06): revenue $647m, FY raised, but stock -12.52% (next-quarter EBITDA guide $72-77m vs $119m Q1). Beats on this line have been bought or sold depending on the guide, not on the beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the guide is public and consensus tracks it. What is not priced is the size of the beat over a mid-quarter reset; if the market expected a Q2-sized 5% beat, the whisper EPS would sit far above $0.15 and the stock would not be 12.6% under its high.
evidence.independence: Q2 guide-vs-actual from the company's Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000035/ex991q126.htm) and Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm). Same company, different documents.

evidence.text: The FY2026 guide of $2.76-2.77bn revenue and $481-489m adj. EBITDA, less Q1 ($647m / $119m), Q2 ($670m / $102m) and the Q3 guide ($705m / $117-120m), implies Q4 revenue of $738-748m (~26% y/y, a deceleration from ~30% in Q3) and Q4 adj. EBITDA of ~$140-151m, a ~19-20% margin against 15-17% in Q2-Q3. The Q4 guide must hold a steep EBITDA ramp; the 10% workforce reduction and easing Prime cash-back rewards cost support it, but a Q4 EBITDA guide below the implied ramp is the setup that cost -12.5% after Q1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: FY revenue raised but next-quarter EBITDA guide implied margin compression, stock -12.52%. Q4 2025 print (2026-02-25): 2026 outlook above expectations, +13.55%. Q2 2026: third FY raise, +20.56%. The guide line has decided the sign on every print in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: The implied Q4 is arithmetic on public numbers, so the level is known; what is not known is whether management guides Q4 inside it or raises again (it has raised the FY three times). Revenue deceleration to ~26% leaves room for a raise; the EBITDA ramp leaves room for a disappointment. The +10.65 put skew is consistent with the market pricing the EBITDA risk.
evidence.independence: Q1 and Q2 actuals from the company's own 8-K exhibits (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000035/ex991q126.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm); restructuring savings from the Aug 5 8-K (https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2026/08/294636-consumer-fintech-chime-to-slash-10-of-workforce-due-to-ai-driven-efficiencies/). Rewards cost easing in H2 from a call summary (https://www.stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/CHYM/2026/Q2), secondary. Shares the Sep 8 document with finding 1 but lands on a different line.

evidence.text: Chime agreed on 2026-09-08 to buy partner bank Stride Bank for $590m cash (~1.5x tangible book), immediately EPS-accretive with >$100m of net synergies (partner-bank fees and funding costs), closing H1 2027 subject to OCC/Fed approval; the call is the first chance to quantify synergy timing and any 2027 framing, while the company says it will keep assets under $10bn to preserve the Durbin exemption.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement itself moved the stock ~+10% after hours and ~+11% premarket on 2026-09-09 (https://www.americanbanker.com/payments/news/chime-to-buy-longtime-partner-stride-bank-for-590-million). No prior print has carried this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The headline is priced (the +10% on announcement). Only incremental detail on synergy phasing or approval progress is new; if the market expected a detailed 2027 synergy bridge on this call the stock would not sit 12.6% under its September high.
evidence.independence: American Banker (https://www.americanbanker.com/payments/news/chime-to-buy-longtime-partner-stride-bank-for-590-million) and the $10bn asset-cap remark via fintech.global (https://fintech.global/2026/09/09/chime-to-acquire-stride-bank-for-590m/).

evidence.text: SoFi's Q3 2026 release (late October, after Chime last spoke) showed a record 1.2m member adds to 17.1m (+35% y/y), deposits +$5.8bn q/q to $51.3bn, Financial Services revenue +25%, a raised FY guide and a 2027 outlook above estimates: the closest listed consumer-fintech peer saw no slowdown in Q3 member acquisition or deposit demand.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of Chime reacting to peer prints; Chime's member-add line drove the +20.56% Q2 reaction (record 1.7m net adds over 12 months).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is +8.8% over a month. SoFi skews to a higher-income member base than Chime, so the read-through to Chime's mass-market members is indirect and was not translated into Chime estimates (consensus still equals the Sep guide).
evidence.independence: Proxy, not a Chime number. The Bancorp's Q3 card volume (finding 5) points the same way from a different document.

evidence.text: The Bancorp (TBBK), one of Chime's two partner banks, reported on 2026-10-29 Q3 gross dollar volume on prepaid, debit and credit cards of $54.3bn vs $44.0bn a year earlier (+23%), fintech-fee-driven EPS of $1.53, and average deposits $8.42bn, flat q/q; card volume growth in the low 20s is consistent with Chime's purchase-volume trend, flat deposits a mild caution.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record; Chime's purchase-volume line was cited in the +20.56% Q2 reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Bancorp does not break out Chime, so no aggregator maps its GDV to Chime estimates; it is a counterparty that spoke after Chime last did. If the market had read it as a Chime beat signal, consensus revenue would have moved above the $705m guide.
evidence.independence: Proxy (a partner bank's portfolio-wide volume, not Chime's). SoFi (finding 4) is a separate document pointing the same way.

evidence.text: Visa's fiscal Q4 2026 release (2026-10-27) showed payments volume +9% in constant dollars and management described October volume growth as relatively stable: no sign of a broad US consumer-spending slowdown into Chime's quarter-end and Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Macro, broadly known and priced; US debit growth specifically was not extractable. Filed small as macro-to-company transmission.
evidence.independence: October stability comment via Benzinga summary (https://benzinga.com/z/48499513), secondary.

evidence.text: The stock ran +6.58% intraday on the print day itself (to $30.06 at 13:02 ET, from $28.20), +4.86% over 5 days and +8.13% over 20, into a +10.65 vol-point put skew; with short interest a moderate 7.58% of float (5.8 days to cover, falling), the run-up raises the bar for the guide without a squeeze cushion of size.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No run-up-conditioned history in the baseline; the two largest down reactions (-14.68%, -12.52%) came on guide disappointments.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; it is filed so the judges see that the entry spot already includes a same-day rally with no identified cause (no news found for 2026-11-04).
evidence.independence: Short interest from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CHYM/short-interest); skew from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: Insiders have sold about $1.2bn across 112 filings over 12 months with no open-market purchases; October sales were small 10b5-1 trades by co-founder Ryan King (50,000 shares at ~$29.40 on 2026-10-09; 11,318 at $31.03 on 2026-10-20 under a plan adopted 2025-08-28), CEO Britt sold under a plan in late August/early September.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Pre-scheduled plan sales carry little information and are public; filed for completeness as a supply overhang.
evidence.independence: Aggregate from Massive.com (https://massive.com/quote/chym).

evidence.text: Q3 GAAP results carry $16-20m of net cash restructuring charges from the ~10% workforce cut (partly offset by a $9-12m SBC reversal, net income hit $6-9m, roughly $0.02 a share), excluded from adj. EBITDA; a GAAP EPS headline against the $0.09 consensus could read light if estimates do not include it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a restructuring charge.
evidence.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the Aug 5 8-K and known; the only unpriced element is headline mechanics if some EPS estimates exclude it. The savings path to the Q4 margin is in finding 2.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview cites the same charge (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/CHYM/21805).

evidence.text: Credit is the watch line in the quarter: MyPay limits were raised to $1,000 with management expecting loss rates to tick up modestly (Q2 MyPay loss rate 0.9% on $4.5bn originations), and Instant Loans (originations +70% q/q to $300m in Q2) are guided to exit Q3 above a $100m revenue run rate.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No credit miss in the baseline; Compass Point initiated at Neutral citing credit risk (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/chime-initiated-with-a-neutral-at-compass-point-on-credit-risk-thefly), undated in results.
evidence.why_not_priced: Management pre-flagged a modest uptick, so a modest rise is priced; only a larger-than-modest move in MyPay losses would be new. No primary data on Q3 losses was found.
evidence.independence: Q2 MyPay figures from the company's Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm).

evidence.text: The CFO seat is still interim (Mark Troughton, President and interim CFO since 2026-08-07 after Matt Newcomb left); a permanent appointment or its absence may be addressed on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO departure was announced with the Q2 print, which rose 20.56%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Known; no new search news found. [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: Stride Bank acquisition closing and OCC/Fed approval expected H1 2027; synergies (>$100m net) accrue after close.

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 revenue consensus $82.41m and EPS -$0.37 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-28, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/EOSE/22089), against the company's own pre-release of $82-83m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001805077/000162828026066229/q326prerelease_101926xfo.htm). The revenue bar is effectively the pre-release. For FY2026 the company guides to the lower half of $300-350m; Street FY revenue is about $309m (one source, Earnings Whispers), so the implied Q4 bar is about $101m against YTD revenue of about $208.3m (Q1 $57.0m + Q2 $68.8m + Q3 midpoint $82.5m). The EPS bar is distorted by fair-value marks and is not the trading line.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 139.27m shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up from 134.85m (09-30) and 120.0m (09-15): about 38.2% of 364.17m shares outstanding, with 4.70 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/eose/shortinterest, FINRA data). As a share of float it is far higher, because Cerberus affiliates hold about 35% and Hudson Bay about 9.2% (S-3ASR of 2026-08-31). The next FINRA release is 2026-11-10, after the window. The 25-delta skew is -30.17 vol points (calls over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call open-interest ratio 0.65, ATM IV 233.6%, event-implied move 17.73%. Tape: spot $2.26, 5-day +15.9%, 20-day -27.1%, -88% from the 52-week high. The stock printed $1.82 on 2026-10-28 (Earnings Whispers) and has bounced about 24% into the print.

evidence.text: The FY2026 guide in the 10-19 pre-release (lower half of $300-350m) needs Q4 revenue of $92-117m against Q3's $82-83m: an 11-42% sequential step-up, in the quarter Line 1 consolidates into Thorn Hill and the final shift is added. Street FY of about $309m implies Q4 of about $101m. The guide has already been cut once (Aug: $300-400m to $300-350m) and then moved to the lower half (Oct). A third trim below $300m, or soft Q4/2027 commentary on the call, is the main downside line. Reaffirming the low end three weeks into Q4 is the base case.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 5, 2026 full release cut the FY guide after the July pre-release had already given revenue: -12.18% on the day and -46.9% drift since (Earnings Whispers). Feb 26, 2026: Q4 revenue miss and weak outlook, -39.44%. When the July pre-release gave no guide, the stock moved +1.86%; the 10-19 pre-release that set 'lower half' moved -0.55%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 'lower half' language is priced: the stock fell from about $3.06 at end-September to $1.82 by 10-28. What is not priced is whether the full release holds $300m or trims again. If the market expected a trim, the skew would favour puts, not calls at -30 vol points, and shorts would not be adding 4.4m shares into 10-15 while calls were bid.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/EOSE/22089, 2026-10-28) independently computes that about $100m in Q4 is needed for the low end and flags repeated slips in the positive-margin target. The Aug 5 guide cut is in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001805077/000162828026052903/eoseq2fy26earningsreleas.htm).

evidence.text: Q3 cash fell only $20m to about $344m, and only because of an $87.0m DOE advance (funded 2026-09-10) and $114m of operating inflows from deposits, milestones and tax-credit collections. Ex-DOE, the drawdown was about $107m in the quarter, including $35m capex. About $99.5m of the $277.5m DOE facility remains, and the Cerberus credit agreement carries a $15m minimum-liquidity covenant. The company has raised repeatedly: a $225m convert, and a $150m rights offering in July 2026. A new raise or financing announced with or around the release is a live possibility. Asked what it would buy: a ramp that is real in revenue (+20% QoQ) but still loses about 54 cents of gross margin per revenue dollar, while backlog fell QoQ. So the sign is mildly negative, not distress: there is no going-concern language in the Q2 10-Q.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 rights offering: Stifel cut its target $12 to $10 (Jul 13, https://finviz.com/news/367612/eos-energy-shares-edge-lower-after-stifel-reduces-price-target-following-capital-raise-eose). An earlier $225m convert pricing saw the stock 'slide further' (Seeking Alpha headline, https://seekingalpha.com/news/4453809-eos-energy-slides-further-after-pricing-225-million-convertible-note-offering, undated in snippet). No financing was announced on any of the print days in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: The cash number is in the pre-release, but the ex-DOE burn arithmetic is not in the wire summary, which led with 'cash about $344m'. A market that had priced an imminent raise at $2 would show put demand; the skew shows the opposite.
evidence.independence: The Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1805077/000162828026052906/eose-20260630.htm) shows six-month operating outflow of $191.8m and $70.5m of capex, consistent with a ~$100m/quarter burn. It shares the 10-19 8-K with the guidance finding for the cash figure only.

evidence.text: Q3 GAAP net income will carry a large non-cash fair-value gain. The stock fell from $5.88 (Jun 30) to $3.06 (Sep 30), and the warrant liabilities ($135.4m plus $254.0m related-party at Jun 30) and derivative liabilities are marked to the period-end price. In Q2 a 19% rise cost about $184m of fair-value losses; in Q1 a 57% fall produced $601.9m of gains and diluted EPS of +$0.12. The headline GAAP EPS is therefore likely far above the -$0.37 consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (May 13): net income $508.9m from fair-value gains, a GAAP 'beat' against a loss consensus; the stock moved +2.22% on the day and gapped down the next (MarketBeat 2026-05-14). The market looked through it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of -$0.37 does not reflect the mark, so headline scrapers and retail will see an EPS 'beat'. Holders know the mechanism and it has no path to the guide, so it is [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Q2 10-Q fair-value schedule (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1805077/000162828026052906/eose-20260630.htm). Monthly closes from https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/EOSE/price.

evidence.text: Backlog fell from a record $807m (Jun 30) to about $765m (Sep 30), so book-to-bill was below 1. The pre-release also says a $100m order under the existing FPUSA capacity reservation did not add to QoQ backlog growth. The call will be asked for order flow; the falling backlog is already public.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's record backlog (+25% QoQ) arrived with the guide cut, and the stock fell -12.18%: the backlog did not carry the print. The 10-19 pre-release with a lower backlog moved -0.55%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced; it was in the pre-release and the stock fell after it. What remains open is Q4 order intake commentary, which only the call can show.
evidence.independence: Q2 backlog of $807m is in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001805077/000162828026052903/eoseq2fy26earningsreleas.htm). Shares the 10-19 document with the guidance finding.

evidence.text: This is a crowded short going into a print whose numbers are mostly pre-released. 139.3m shares were short at 10-15 (about 38% of shares outstanding, rising for three straight settlements; 4.7 days to cover), and the float is much smaller because Cerberus holds about 35%. The 25-delta skew is -30 vol points (upside paid). The stock has bounced about 24% off its $1.82 low (10-28) into the print. Absent a new negative such as a guide trim or a raise, a 'no surprise' release gives shorts a reason to cover.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 9, 2026: +29.63% (baseline, 8-K 2.02 day). The stock spiked about 20% intraday that day (low-quality auto-generated page, used only for the date), showing the name can squeeze. Equibles' screening index rates the squeeze score 73/100, which is not a probability.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the skew and the 5-day bounce show some squeeze has already been bid. If it were fully priced, short interest would already have fallen. Equibles' model expects only a ~5% drop at the 10-30 settlement, which leaves most of the short in place.
evidence.independence: Sealed baseline skew_25d_vol_points -30.17 and run_up_5d_pct +15.9 (option and tape data, a different source from FINRA). Earnings Whispers 10-28 gives the $1.82 low.

evidence.text: Q3 gross margin of -53% to -55% improved 16-18 points QoQ, the eighth straight improvement. The CFO says there is 'a clear path to positive margins', and consolidation into Thorn Hill (final shift in Q4) is said to lower cost per unit. If the full release or call dates positive gross margin, say Q4 2026 or H1 2027, that is the one unambiguous upside line still unpublished.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin improvement has printed every quarter: Q1 -78%, Q2 -71%, Q3 about -54%. The stock still fell on two of the three full releases this year. Earnings Whispers notes the positive-margin target has slipped repeatedly, so the market has learned to discount it.
evidence.why_not_priced: No date for positive margin has been given (the Q2 release gave none). A dated target would be new, but a history of slippage limits how much it is paid.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/EOSE/22089) on repeated slips of the margin target. Shares the 10-19 document with the guidance and backlog findings.

evidence.text: Revenue quality: in Q2, $55.0m of $68.8m (80%) was related-party revenue from a project contributed to Frontier Power USA. FPUSA is the Cerberus/Hudson Bay JV in which Eos holds a minority stake. It also held about half of backlog, and the $100m Blanquilla PO came under its capacity reservation. The Q3 10-Q will show how much of the $82-83m is again related-party, which the pre-release does not disclose.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 release disclosed the 80% related-party share alongside the guide cut, and the stock fell -12.18%. The effect of each item alone is not separable.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q2 concentration is known. The Q3 mix is not public until the 10-Q, and a market that had priced a further rise would not be bidding calls. Net of the rest: the non-FPUSA customers (six POs from six customers in Q3) would need to show growth to offset.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/EOSE/22089) independently says about 80% of last quarter's revenue and about half of backlog came from FPUSA.

evidence.text: Insider and management churn: CCO Michelle Buczkowski sold 50,000 shares at a $2.00 weighted average on 2026-10-29 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-12-11 to cover RSU tax withholding. Outgoing CCO Nathan Kroeker left on 2026-10-20. Neither is an informative signal on the print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None identifiable.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public on EDGAR. The sale is mechanical tax withholding and carries no information.
evidence.independence: 8-K of 2026-08-25 on the CCO transition (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1805077/000162828026058890/eose-20260824.htm).

evidence.text: Resale overhang: an S-3ASR (2026-08-31) registers 56.5m shares for resale by Cerberus (37.4m) and Hudson Bay (19.1m) from the Frontier warrants, exchange rights and Series B conversion. Hudson Bay is a typical seller. This is a supply overhang with no dated catalyst in the window.
The next FINRA short-interest release (10-30 settlement) is due 2026-11-10, after the exit window.

evidence.text: Joby's three 2026 operating targets are unconfirmed as of 2026-11-04 with eight weeks left: first passengers in 2026, a Dubai launch before year-end, and two additional aircraft deliveries. Every press release since the Q2 letter (eIPP Texas 9/10, cross-country 9/18, Florida 10/30, Air Force 11/4) is silent on Dubai, GCAA aircraft approval and passengers. The Q3 letter has to reaffirm these targets or slip them to 2027.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print (first-passenger and Dubai target reaffirmed, revenue beat) gained +21.2%. The Q2 print (targets reaffirmed, guide raised) gained +5.5%. The 2025-08 print fell -8.9%. No release in the baseline slipped these targets outright.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. A 68% drawdown and Barclays' $4 target (Oct 9) already discount execution risk, and a Fool piece on Oct 30 named Dubai as the catalyst with slip risk. evidence.independence: Dubai launch 'before end of 2026' still depends on GCAA aircraft approval (Fool 2026-10-30, https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/30/joby-aviations-dubai-launch-is-the-1-catalyst-that/). The vertiport was GCAA-certified in July 2026 (https://www.agbi.com/aviation/2026/07/dubais-first-vertiport-is-given-operational-clearance/). evidence.text: Joby put a $750M at-the-market program in place on 2026-08-11 (424B5 filed 2026-08-14). The Q3 10-Q will disclose how much was sold at $5-8. Stocktitan shows 993.9M shares outstanding, against about 930M implied by a $4.82B market cap at $5.19. The money funds Resonant Sciences (about $450-500M, mostly cash, closing early 2027) and H2 burn of $385-415M, against $2.3B of cash at 6/30. That is a defence build-out and runway, not distress.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock slipped on dilution fears after the ATM was filed (StocksToTrade, 2026-08-18). After the Q3 2025 print, which came with a $500M+ offering, the stock fell -4.5% (baseline 2025-11-05).
evidence.why_not_priced: The facility is known, but the amount sold is not; it surfaces in the 10-Q. A large Q3 sale near the lows would read as dilution at the bottom. Had the market priced heavy usage, short interest would not still be rising into the print.
evidence.independence: The Davis Polk deal note confirms the $750M size (https://www.davispolk.com/experience/joby-aviation-750-million-market-offering). The Resonant Sciences cash use is in the Aug 11 release (https://ir.jobyaviation.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/189/joby-aviation-to-scale-defense-business-through-acquisition).

evidence.text: A federal jury awarded Aerosonic $116.9M against Joby in a trade-secrets case on 2026-10-02/06; Joby is challenging it. If Q3 accrues it as a recognised subsequent event, GAAP loss per share widens by about $0.12 against the -$0.25 consensus and the headline reads as a miss. Joby is appealing and may argue the loss is not probable.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The verdict itself cost about 8% to a new 52-week low on 2026-10-09. No prior print carried a litigation accrual.
evidence.why_not_priced: The verdict is priced, since the stock already fell on it. What is not visible is whether consensus EPS includes an accrual. The two aggregators both sit at -$0.25, unchanged by a $0.12 charge, which suggests it does not. The item is non-cash and below the operating line, with no path to guidance, so it is sized as a fraction of its dollars.
evidence.independence: The tikr piece of 2026-10-13 says Joby asked the court to overturn the verdict (https://www.tikr.com/blog/joby-aviation-stock-has-lost-61-this-year-heres-why-barclays-doubts-its-factory-can-keep-up). This finding shares the GAAP-EPS line with the remeasurement finding, which offsets it.

evidence.text: Q2 2026 GAAP results carried a $108M non-cash charge for the fair value of warrants and earn-out shares, because the stock rose in Q2. The stock then fell roughly 19.8% in July and was near $6.45 by 9/20. Any instrument still marked to market at 9/30 therefore gives Q3 a non-cash gain that flatters GAAP EPS against -$0.25.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $108M charge produced a GAAP EPS miss of $0.02 (MarketBeat 2026-08-05), and the stock still gained +5.5%. The market looked through the line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Aggregator consensus EPS rarely models mark-to-market lines. If the gain were in the estimates, they would have risen as the stock fell; Chartmill shows Q3 EPS estimates revised DOWN over three months. The remaining liability is uncertain: NYSE filed a Form 25 on 2026-08-11, possibly the public warrants delisting at the 5-year expiry.
evidence.independence: July -19.8%: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/10/why-joby-aviation-stock-plummeted-198-in-july-but/. Down 54% YTD by 9/20: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/20/joby-aviation-stock-is-down-54-this-year-heres-why/. This finding shares the trefis document with the verdict finding, and the two roughly offset.

evidence.text: Joby issued 2,419,801 earn-out shares on 2026-09-10 because Blade's acquired passenger operations hit their 12-month EBITDA milestones. Q3 is Blade's seasonal peak (summer routes), Blade already beat Q2 revenue by 27% ($38.6M vs about $30.2M), and Q3 revenue consensus is $38-40M. That makes a revenue beat more likely than not.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat on revenue: +21.2%. Q2 2026 beat revenue by 27% but missed EPS by $0.02: +5.5%. The name has paid for revenue beats, but revenue is not the line it trades on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The earn-out 8-K is a resale-prospectus item that no preview cites. Revenue estimates were revised up 9.6% in three months (Chartmill), so part of this is in the bar. A fully priced beat would mean consensus above the $40M top of Q2-plus-seasonality, and it is not.
evidence.independence: Q2 beat versus $30.2M: https://www.tikr.com/blog/joby-aviation-stock-has-lost-61-this-year-heres-why-barclays-doubts-its-factory-can-keep-up. Caveat: the FY guide of $115-125M implies only $52-62M for H2, so a strong Q3 may simply come at Q4's expense, which is why this is sized small.

evidence.text: Centrus closed the Westerman Holdings acquisition on 2026-10-19 for about $116M ($95M cash, $21M stock), and the 2026-09-09 prospectus supplement says the target had about $160M of revenue in 2025. Westerman serves non-nuclear oil-and-gas customers as well as Centrus. Consolidating it from Oct 19 adds roughly $20-30M of external Q4 revenue that the reaffirmed $450-500M FY guide (set before the deal) and the Street's $470.6M likely do not include, so a raised or firmed FY revenue range on the call is plausible.

Earnings Whispers' 10-27 preview still carries FY consensus of $470.6M against the old guide. If the market had priced a mechanical revenue add, FY consensus would sit above the guide midpoint.
evidence.independence: Two documents from the same company: the 424B5 for the revenue and the 8-K for the close and the oil-and-gas customer base. No independent source. The revenue is inorganic and low-margin, and the market may look through it.

evidence.text: Q2 2026 already showed cost pressure that carries into a seasonally light Q3 (consensus revenue $55-59M against $176.1M in Q2): SWU unit cost +13% y/y against SWU price +3%, Technical Solutions at a $1.7M gross loss, and net hiring targets raised to 175+ at Piketon and 100+ at Oak Ridge. UBS cut its target to $170 on higher operating costs, and Needham cut to $206 on earnings concerns. Q3 is therefore likely a GAAP loss or near-zero EPS against a bar that ranges from +$0.35 to -$0.75.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-05), the last seasonally light quarter, reported diluted EPS of $0.19 against a $0.36 consensus and fell 14.72%. Q2 2026 beat on revenue and EPS and still fell 5.12%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The cost lines are public, the stock is -38% over 20 days, and the EPS bar is so dispersed that no single miss is defined. It is filed small and capped because the bar is disputed.
evidence.independence: The analyst target cuts are reported at https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/centrus-energy-stock-hits-52week-low-at-968-usd-93CH-4992590 (2026-11-02) and in the Barchart UBS item. Both rest on the same Q2 cost lines, so this is one finding.

evidence.text: DOE said it does not intend to exercise further options on the HALEU Operation Contract. Its period of performance ran only to 2026-09-30 under a $15.0M fixed-price 3-month Option 1b with no production, and the proposed FY2027 DOE budget excludes it. About $0.8B of Technical Solutions backlog is exposed, and the Q3 10-Q is the first report after the expiry, so it will show whether that backlog is cut or converted into a commercial operating arrangement.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The DOE non-exercise language first appeared in the 2026-08-05 release, and the stock fell 5.12% that session alongside the other items.
evidence.why_not_priced: The risk is disclosed. What is not public is the treatment: a $0.8B backlog write-down would make the reported backlog fall even as LEU bookings rise. Size is net of the rest of the company: Technical Solutions was about $23M of Q2's $176M.
evidence.independence: ANS / Power coverage of the contract restructuring: https://www.ans.org/news/2026-07-06/article-8180/doe-contract-boosts-centruss-haleu-goals-as-urenco-continues-leu-expansion/

evidence.text: Sanofi's Q3 2026 release puts its influenza and COVID-19 vaccine sales at EUR1,256m, down 18.8% at CER: US EUR911m (-13.4%), Europe EUR243m (-32.0%). It says Northern Hemisphere seasonal deliveries are phased toward Q4 this year, and its Oct 6 aide-memoire blames 'atypical strain selection timelines'. Nuvaxovid is sold by Sanofi and pays Novavax high-teens to low-twenties royalties plus supply sales. Those Sanofi lines are excluded from Novavax's revenue framework and are the unguided part of the Q3 number, which suggests Q3 Sanofi royalties and supply sales tilt low against Q3 2025, when the Sanofi line was $48m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sanofi royalties have been tiny so far: $0.7m in Q2 2026 and $4.2m in H1 per the 10-Q. The last two big up-moves (+17.4% Feb 2026, +15.6% May 2026) came on framework beats and raises, not on Sanofi lines. A 2026 framework raise in Aug bought +0.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus for NVAX Q3 revenue ranges from $50.6m to $78.7m, and the Chartmill figure has been cut 22.5% in three months, so part of this is probably in the lower estimates. No NVAX preview I found cites Sanofi's Q4 phasing. If it were priced, the estimates would agree near the low end and the previews would mention Sanofi's phasing.
evidence.independence: Sanofi's own Q3 aide-memoire (2026-10-06) says the same about phasing: https://www.sanofi.com/assets/dotcom/content-app/events/quaterly-results/2026/2026-q3-2026-results/20261006-Sanofi-Q3-2026-Aide-memoire.pdf. It is the same company and the same fact, so it counts once. Phasing to Q4 also means the shortfall partly reverses next quarter, which is why this is small.

evidence.text: Pfizer's Q3 2026 release (Nov 3) reports US Comirnaty revenue of $562m, down 35% from $870m, 'primarily resulting from narrower vaccine recommendations'. The 2026-27 formula is approved only for adults 65+ and high-risk people aged 5-64, and there is no functioning ACIP recommendation (AJMC, 2026-10-01). This is an independent read on the US COVID vaccine market for the 2026-27 season, on which Sanofi's Nuvaxovid sales, and so Novavax's royalties and any commentary on the US season, depend. Pfizer released after Novavax last spoke.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no separable precedent. The stock fell on the Nov 2025 print (-1.3%) when COVID vaccine weakness under US policy was the theme, and the Feb 2025 print (-3.55%) also came on a weak COVID outlook.
evidence.why_not_priced: Pfizer reported only one session before this print, and NVAX closed +7% on Nov 4 (equibles snapshot), so the market did not visibly mark NVAX down on the peer's US number. If priced, NVAX would have weakened after Nov 3, and previews would ask about the US season rather than only the milestones.
evidence.independence: This is a proxy, a peer product, and Novavax and Sanofi have not confirmed the transmission. Sanofi's Q3 shows US flu/COVID down 13.4% (a separate source, same direction), but Sanofi attributes that to timing rather than demand. The AJMC piece on there being no functioning ACIP is here: https://www.ajmc.com/view/who-recommends-covid-19-vaccines-without-acip-goad-pharmd

evidence.text: The 8-K of Oct 29 records that Sanofi dosed the fifth patient in the EU Phase 3 flu-COVID combination trial on Oct 28, 2026. That triggers a $125m milestone to Novavax, about 49% of the $255m framework midpoint, with payment expected by Q1 2027. It is Q4 revenue, not Q3, and is excluded from the framework. On the call it can lift FY2026 total revenue and the cash runway and settle doubts about Sanofi's commitment after its CEO change.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier Sanofi milestone news moved the stock strongly: +19% on the May 2025 $175m BLA approval milestone. This one was anticipated. Reports of EU regulators clearing the trial ran from about Oct 12 (finanztrends), and the stock fell from $12.82 (Oct 15) to about $9.6 (Oct 22) anyway, then sat near $10.3 around the Oct 29 announcement.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it has been public for a week and expected for three. What is not priced is how management folds it into a total-revenue figure, the 2026 cash path and the profitability timeline. The framework excludes Sanofi milestones, so consensus models may not carry it in FY2026. If fully priced, the stock would have re-rated on Oct 29, and it did not.
evidence.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-29) flags the CIC milestone and Sanofi's continued interest as the key questions: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NVAX/22450. Contract Pharma covers the trial start (2026-10-29).
